editorial:
Imagine being the oldest kid in an orphanage and basically becoming the big brother to everyone there. That is exactly where you find Norman, a sweet guy who spends all his time making sure the younger kids are happy and safe at Greenwood Home. The movie has a really warm, cozy feeling at first, especially when the group takes a trip to Brighton. You will love seeing Norman's reaction to the ocean since he has never seen the sea before. It is a simple, feel-good setup that makes you root for these kids immediately.

What really makes this flick work is the battle between the innocent kids and the mean property developer. The pacing is snappy, and the comedy comes from the clever ways the children fight back against the adults. While some of the acting is a bit over-the-top, it fits the era perfectly. If you are looking for a lighthearted story about teamwork, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The kids and Norman use their wits to stop the greedy chairman from tearing down their home. They manage to expose his bad intentions and trick him into a situation where he cannot go through with his factory plan. In the end, the orphanage is saved, and the villain is defeated. The movie wraps up with the children safely back in their home, knowing they have a bright and secure future together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic family comedies and underdog stories.
